final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record in narrower, more careful terms. That reframing is useful, but it does not satisfy the missing policy predicate. The policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The available record, as summarized to this role, still indicates a material subgroup regression and still lacks attached approved mitigation, owner-approved risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language for that weakness. That means the Actor's narrowed position may describe a path to compliant_with_caveats if those artifacts exist or are added and approved, but it does not establish that the present record is compliant now. The distinction matters: a caveated position can be enough only when the caveat is already satisfied in the current evidence set, not when the caveat names a missing compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation actually reflects the current evaluation results for this release.
No new admissible evidence shows approved disclosure text for the fraud dispute review subgroup weakness.
No new admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or reviewed owner-approved risk acceptance tied to this release.

The policy makes current-release documentation plus disclosure or approved mitigation a compliance predicate; aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy that predicate by themselves.
Prior approval and informal monitoring remain contextual only and cannot carry current-release certification.
